optional_codes.reason: Dietary counseling and surveillance: a registered dietitian saw her at the same visit, started a supplement and set a diet review. Against it, the dietitian's note records an assessment and a plan more than counseling, and nothing requires the code. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Protein-calorie malnutrition of moderate and mild degree: reporting a code from this category takes the malnutrition diagnosis from the dietitian's note. The provider documents no malnutrition.
Unspecified severe protein-calorie malnutrition: the same assumption.
Unspecified protein-calorie malnutrition: a less specific code for a diagnosis that the provider did not make.

citations.K90.0: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Section I.B.14: code assignment is based on the documentation by the patient's provider, the physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner legally accountable for establishing the patient's diagnosis; the listed exceptions, for which another clinician's documentation may be used, do not include malnutrition, and for the listed items the associated diagnosis must still be documented by the patient's provider. Here the gastroenterologist's diagnosis is celiac disease, well controlled on a gluten-free diet; the diagnosis of moderate protein-calorie malnutrition appears only in the registered dietitian's note, so celiac disease is reported alone.

coder_notes: The two parts of the note disagree: the gastroenterologist records a well controlled condition with no symptoms, and the dietitian records three months of halved intake. Section I.B.14 says that with conflicting documentation from different clinicians the patient's provider is queried. The reduced intake is reported only in the dietitian's note and is not coded. Celiac disease is a current condition under dietary treatment, so no follow-up examination code is used. The test results are normal. No body mass index is recorded. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
